Not to mention that vapors containing irritants and carcinogens can still act as irritants and carcinogens even if you can't visibly see them in the air.

EDIT: Clarity, fixed a grammatical error.
Ingredients in vaping liquids water, propylene glycol and/or vegetable glycerin, nicotine, and food safe flavorings.

They generally contain or produce other toxic chemical components. As seen here and here.

Hell, even the unique shape of the molecules in e-cigs could represent an additional cancer risk (in the way that certain types of asbestos cause lung cancer and others don't).

3rd hand exposure is also elevated with the use of e-cigs compared to traditional ones.

I'm not trying to be combative here, only trying to point out that e-cigs do represent a health risk, and that every study done on them finds more evidence of their dangers.

P.S. - Most studies indicate that e-cig use doesn't help people get off of smoking, they just substitute and/or move back and forth from one to the other.
Why would someone buy their ingredients to make their e-liquid without verified 3rd party testing? They should be made as safe a possible to use as an alternative.

Currently, there is just very little oversight or regulation for e-cigs, and some of these harmful chemicals are byproducts of safer chemicals present in the liquid used.

Researchers are even finding evidence that without the presence of such chemicals, some e-cigs may still represent a danger to the lining of the lungs. The particulate matter that is produced as the spray that users breath in can be much smaller than typical moisture/chemical combinations in the air. Meaning they can interact the lungs in a different way than it would if it was just breathed in as normal air and water vapor, and cause irritation.

Studies have already shown this can be the case with some e-cigs, leading some to suspect that such vapors could lead to cancer, even without the presence of many traditional carcinogens.

If you are a regular user, you should probably be aware of these factors, and keep them in mind. It took decades to study the health effects of regular cigarettes, so we have a ways to go before the true health impact of e-cigs is well understood.
